The needle slips on the first try. The pencil lifts halfway through the second try. The first few attempts do not look like circles at all. Using a compass for the first time is all about practice. They erase the broken lines, adjust their grip, and try again. The curiosity keeps them trying until the two ends of the line finally meet perfectly.

Belonging creates ownership. Ownership creates responsibility. Responsibility creates nation-builders. We are proud to share that our Principal, Mrs. Pavani Dokka, has been featured among the 50 Visionary Principals: Leading Education into a New Era of Learning in Times School, circulated with The Times of India, Hyderabad. Her piece, "From 'My School' to 'My Country'," speaks to something she believes deeply: children grow into responsible citizens when they learn to belong, care, and take ownership of the spaces they share. A fallen notebook was picked up. A fan switched off in an empty classroom. A senior who stays back to help a junior. Small acts, learned early, that shape the nation our children will build. We see this conviction in her every day. Often the first to arrive and the last to leave, she gives her time and energy to our students, parents, teachers, and everyone who makes Tatva what it is. Congratulations, Pavani Ma'am.
